## One preparation layer, three reporting pathways

The three routine analytical workflows share the same data-preparation pathway.

Although the first three actions appear under **Update dashboard** in the Stata menu, they do more than prepare dashboard data. **Dashboard Steps 1-3 are the common analytical preparation layer for the wider BNR reporting system.**

[Dashboard Step 3](dashboards/create-analysis-inputs.qmd) is the main branch point. It creates the private deidentified analytical datasets used by the downstream workflows.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["REDCap monthly release"] --> B["Dashboard Step 1<br/>Private REDCap extract"]
    B --> C["Dashboard Step 2<br/>Confidential cumulative dataset"]
    C --> D["Dashboard Step 3<br/>Deidentified analytical inputs"]

    D --> E["Dashboard metrics<br/>Steps 4-6"]
    D --> F["Tabulations<br/>Steps 1-3"]
    D --> G["Routine briefings<br/>Steps 1-3"]

    E --> H["Approved public outputs"]
    F --> H
    G --> H

    H --> I["Quarto publishing layer"]
    I --> J["BNR Info-Hub"]
```

## How the branches differ

| Workflow | Step 3 input | What the workflow then owns |
|---|---|---|
| **Dashboard metrics** | Purpose-specific metric input, currently `count` for the burden family | Metric calculation, disclosure control, review, approval and metric publication. |
| **Tabulations** | `all_variables` | Seven routine table calculations, table-specific suppression, review, approval and table publication. |
| **Routine briefings** | `count`, `case_fatality` or `length_of_stay`, depending on the briefing | Analyst-owned calculations and figures, human disclosure review, approval and briefing-package publication. |

This separation matters. Tabulations and briefings **do not rebuild the confidential cumulative dataset** and should not repeat the Step 1-3 preparation logic. They start from the approved deidentified products created by Dashboard Step 3.

The Step 3 products remain private. Each downstream workflow is responsible for creating its own reviewable output package and applying the disclosure and approval controls appropriate to that product.

## Ad-hoc briefings

The ad-hoc briefing pathway is deliberately more flexible.

An ad-hoc analysis is created in an analyst-owned DO file rather than through the routine Briefing Step 1 dispatcher. The analyst must declare the source and create the standard private staging package. The package then joins the common briefing controls at **Briefing Step 2: Review and approve** and **Briefing Step 3: Publish**, using the exact ad-hoc package ID.

For registry analyses, use an appropriate approved deidentified analytical source wherever the analysis permits. Any different source must be explicitly recorded in the briefing release metadata.

## Compute and publish remain separate

Stata creates and controls the analytical products. Quarto consumes only approved public products.

Updating narrative pages, listings or other website content is therefore covered under **Operate the Info-Hub**, not inside the analytical workflow chapters.
